title: 2nd Stopping Place 2nd Truth 2nd Example From Sura Al Nahl

questions.question: What helpful thing does this verse teach people about animals like cows, goats, and sheep?
questions.answer: They give clean milk for people to drink.

questions.question: Where does the milk come from inside the animals?
questions.answer: It comes from inside their bodies, between dirty things and blood.

questions.question: What is special about the milk even though it is made in that place?
questions.answer: It stays pure, clean, and good to drink.

questions.question: Which mothers are named in this passage as giving milk?
questions.answer: Animal mothers and human mothers.

questions.question: Besides milk, what loving gift is placed in mothers’ hearts?
questions.answer: Kindness and care for their babies.

questions.question: How does the passage compare a mother’s love with milk?
questions.answer: It says a mother’s love is even better and sweeter.

questions.question: What qualities are needed to make milk and mercy in this careful way?
questions.answer: Mercy, wisdom, knowledge, power, will, and care.

questions.question: According to the passage, can random things or blind forces do this work?
questions.answer: No. They cannot do such careful work.

questions.question: Why not?
questions.answer: Because the work is wise, careful, and perfectly ordered.

questions.question: Where does this amazing care happen?
questions.answer: All over the world.

questions.question: In how many mothers does this care appear?
questions.answer: In countless mothers from many, many kinds of living things.

questions.question: What big truth does this whole example point to?
questions.answer: It shows Allah is One.

questions.question: What does the passage say we can learn from cattle?
questions.answer: We can learn a lesson about Allah’s care and power.

questions.question: What drink is mentioned as coming from these animals?
questions.answer: Milk.

questions.question: What color is the milk described as?
questions.answer: White.

questions.question: What are two things the milk is said to be?
questions.answer: Clean and nourishing.

questions.question: What makes the milk amazing inside the mother’s body?
questions.answer: It comes out clean even though it is near unclean things.

questions.question: What feeling does Allah place in mothers for their young ones?
questions.answer: Tender love.

questions.question: Who receives this tender care?
questions.answer: Their babies.

questions.question: What does this show about how the world is run?
questions.answer: It is run with mercy and wisdom.

questions.question: Which false causes are rejected in the passage?
questions.answer: Chance, mixed-up elements, and blind forces.

questions.question: What idea is repeated about the way this happens in many mothers around the world?
questions.answer: It happens at the same time, in the same careful way.

questions.question: If the same wise care is seen everywhere, what can we understand?
questions.answer: One Creator is doing it.

questions.question: What is the main message of this part?
questions.answer: Clean milk and motherly love are clear signs of Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Which living things are talked about in this passage?
questions.answer: Cows, camels, goats, sheep, and human mothers.

questions.question: What comes from their bodies for people to drink?
questions.answer: Milk.

questions.question: How is the milk described?
questions.answer: It is pure, pleasant, and good for the body.

questions.question: What surprising contrast does the passage point out about the milk?
questions.answer: It is clean even though it is made among things that are not clean.

questions.question: What else, besides milk, is given to mothers?
questions.answer: Loving care in their hearts.

questions.question: Why is that love important?
questions.answer: It helps mothers care for their babies.

questions.question: Does the passage treat this as something small and ordinary or as something amazing?
questions.answer: It treats it as something amazing.

questions.question: What does the passage say is needed for such amazing work?
questions.answer: Great mercy, wisdom, knowledge, power, will, and care.

questions.question: What kinds of things are said to be unable to make this happen?
questions.answer: Wild chance, mixed elements, and blind powers.

questions.question: What clue in the passage shows this work is not random?
questions.answer: It happens with the same wisdom and care in many mothers everywhere.

questions.question: When this happens in countless mothers across the earth, what does it become?
questions.answer: A clear proof.

questions.question: A clear proof of what?
questions.answer: A clear proof that Allah is One.

questions.question: What lesson does the verse give through animals?
questions.answer: It teaches about the clean milk Allah gives people.

questions.question: Why is the milk a sign to think about?
questions.answer: Because it comes out pure from inside the body in an amazing way.

questions.question: What makes the milk good for people?
questions.answer: It is clean, pleasant, and nourishing.

questions.question: Whose bodies are mentioned as giving this milk?
questions.answer: The bodies of certain animals and human mothers.

questions.question: What is found in the hearts of these mothers?
questions.answer: Deep care for their young.

questions.question: How does the passage describe that care compared with milk?
questions.answer: It says the care is even more precious.

questions.question: What does this tell us about the One who made mothers this way?
questions.answer: He is merciful, wise, and powerful.

questions.question: Why can’t blind force be the maker of this?
questions.answer: Blind force cannot plan and care so perfectly.

questions.question: Why can’t chance be the maker of this?
questions.answer: Chance does not make the same careful result again and again.

questions.question: What pattern is seen around the whole world?
questions.answer: The same milk and the same caring love appear in many mothers.

questions.question: What does one shared pattern across the world suggest about the Maker?
questions.answer: It suggests there is one Maker, not many.

questions.question: What belief does this support for a Muslim child?
questions.answer: It supports believing in Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What drink in the passage is made for people from animals?
questions.answer: Milk.

questions.question: Name two animals in the passage that give this milk.
questions.answer: Cows and goats.

questions.question: What is amazing about where the milk is made?
questions.answer: It is made inside the body near things that are dirty, but it stays clean.

questions.question: What second gift is given to mothers besides milk?
questions.answer: Gentle love for their babies.

questions.question: Why is that gentle love a blessing?
questions.answer: It helps the babies be cared for.

questions.question: What does the passage say is required for these gifts to exist?
questions.answer: Mercy, wisdom, knowledge, power, will, and careful planning.

questions.question: Could mixed-up natural things make such a perfect result by themselves?
questions.answer: No. They could not.

questions.question: What kind of work is this passage describing: messy work or orderly work?
questions.answer: Orderly work.

questions.question: How widely is this orderly work seen?
questions.answer: It is seen all across the earth.

questions.question: What does seeing the same careful work in many kinds of mothers teach us?
questions.answer: It teaches that one Lord made them all.

questions.question: Finish the idea: this example is a clear sign of Allah’s _____.
questions.answer: Oneness.

questions.question: What does the passage want us to notice in cattle and mothers?
questions.answer: The gift of milk and the love for their young.

questions.question: How is the milk described in a simple way?
questions.answer: It is clean, white, and good to drink.

questions.question: What makes this milk hard for people to copy?
questions.answer: It is made perfectly in a place inside the body that is not clean.

questions.question: What feeling do mothers have in their hearts for their babies?
questions.answer: Tenderness.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the skill behind making milk and mercy?
questions.answer: It is full of wisdom and care.

questions.question: Which powers are denied any real part in this work?
questions.answer: Chance, the elements, and blind forces.

questions.question: Why are they denied a part?
questions.answer: Because they cannot make such careful, wise, and loving results.

questions.question: What repeated feature makes this proof stronger?
questions.answer: It happens in countless mothers in the same careful way.

questions.question: Does this happen only in one place or everywhere on earth?
questions.answer: Everywhere on earth.

questions.question: What can a student infer from the same wise work happening everywhere?
questions.answer: One Allah is in control of it all.

questions.question: What is the best main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: Milk and motherly love are beautiful signs of Allah’s mercy and oneness.
